steps.heading: std::cout
steps.body: std::cout writes to the console using the << operator.

steps.heading: Full program
steps.body: Every C++ program starts in main().

steps.prompt: Complete the stream object used for console output.

steps.heading: Typed variables
steps.body: C++ is statically typed: you declare the type.

steps.prompt: Declare an integer x equal to 10.

steps.instructions: Print the sum of 2 and 3 (expected output: 5).
Arrange the blocks to print "big" when x is greater than 5.

steps.heading: for loop

steps.instructions: Print 0, 1, 2 each on its own line.
Print the sum of numbers 1 to 5 (expected: 15).

steps.heading: Functions
steps.body: Declare a return type, a name, and parameters.

steps.prompt: Give the function the correct return type for an integer sum.
steps.template: ___ add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }

steps.instructions: Define add(a, b) returning a+b and print add(2, 3). Expected: 5.
Write maximum(a, b) returning the larger value and print maximum(7, 4). Expected: 7.
Count even numbers in {1,2,3,4,5,6} and print it. Expected: 3.

steps.heading: class
steps.body: Classes bundle data and methods. Note the semicolon after the closing brace.

steps.instructions: Assemble a Dog class with a public bark() method returning "Woof".
Create a Dog with bark() returning "Woof" and print Dog().bark(). Expected: Woof.
Print the reverse of "hello". Expected: olleh.

steps.heading: std::string
steps.body: From <string>. Concatenate with + and measure with .size().

steps.prompt: Complete the method that returns a string's length.

steps.instructions: Concatenate "code" and "hero" and print. Expected: codehero.

steps.heading: Pointers
steps.body: A pointer stores an address. & takes an address, * dereferences it.

steps.prompt: Dereference the pointer p to read its value.

steps.instructions: Print the value of x through a pointer. Expected: 42.
x starts at 41. Increment it through a reference and print x. Expected: 42.

steps.heading: <algorithm> & <numeric>
steps.body: std::sort, std::accumulate and friends operate on ranges.

steps.prompt: Complete the algorithm that sorts a range.

steps.instructions: Sum {1,2,3,4} with std::accumulate and print it. Expected: 10.
Sort {3,1,2} ascending and print the first element. Expected: 1.
